messages.author: 8bcb7cabc778c7da
messages.subject: exporting ply files from PCA
parts:
Hi folks,

Could I get some help with coding to export ply files from the extremes of PCA axes? No matter what I put in the writePLY code, it only gives me the mesh for positive PC1. I would like to do this for pos/neg extremes of PC 1 and 2.

PCAsym <- plotTangentSpace(Y.gpasym$coords, groups = Species, pch = 21, warpgrids = TRUE,
                           mesh = refmesh, legend = TRUE) #opens 3D window with PC1 pos & neg
writePLY("PCAsym$pc.shapes$PC1max.ply") #but these 2 lines of code produce the same ply file
writePLY("PCAsym$pc.shapes$PC1min.ply")

Thanks,
Christy

Just a guess!

Cheers!

messages.author: 8bcb7cabc778c7da
messages.subject: Re: exporting ply files from PCA
parts:
From the 1st line of code for plotTangentSpace, I get a window in RGL with rotatable 3D models for PC1 min and max, but trying to export those using any of the following lines (and later appending .ply when necessary to open the file in e.g. Meshlab) still only gives me the mesh for PC1 max

> writePLY("PCAsym.ply")
> writePLY("PCAsym$pc.shapes")
> writePLY("PCAsym$pc.shapes.ply")
> writePLY("PCAsym$pc.shapes$PC1min")

In the meantime I found a workaround using warpRefMesh to take the reference mesh I made using the consensus shape from mshape, and warp it to the coordinates from the different PC axis min/max

> PC1minmesh <- warpRefMesh(refmesh, ref, PCAsym$pc.shapes$PC1min, color=NULL, centered=F)
writePLY("PC1minmesh.ply")

But I'm happy to hear any other suggestions from people working on 3D data!

Best,
Christy

messages.author: 4d71c6e24fb21497
messages.subject: RE: [geomorph-r-package] Re: exporting ply files from PCA
parts:
Christy,

 

I looked at the lines of code you have in this email, and think I see the confusion. While plotTangentSpace shows the meshes, it does not include them in its output.  That is, PCAsym$pc.shapes$PC1min and PCAsym$pc.shapes$PC1max only contain xy (or xyz) coordinates of the landmarks.  So one would still need to shunt these through warpRefMesh to obtain the estimated mesh (and ply) for that specimen.

 

Now, why writePLY from RGL managed to actually create something out of just a set of landmarks is most curious. That should not work as far as I can tell.

Dean
